# MERCY by Shahir Anuar Shahrani

> Author-maintained public information about MERCY, an illustrated Qur’an-inspired Islamic story for young readers, families and educators. This is a book summary and source guide, not the book text or an independent review.

## Direct answer
MERCY by Shahir Anuar Shahrani follows Zayd and his father Khalid through questions about faith, mistakes, learning differently, self-worth, gratitude and compassion. Families and educators can use its public reading guide to discuss Islamic values through the story and connect ideas across subjects.

## The 86-thread, six-lens method
The open guide maps 86 chapter-specific discussion threads. Each thread can be explored through science, history, psychology, ethics, faith and art. This gives young readers a way to practise connecting ideas across fields and polymathic thinking; it does not claim an IQ gain or guarantee an outcome. Ibn Sina (Avicenna) and Leonardo da Vinci are historical inspiration for cross-disciplinary curiosity, not characters or endorsers of the book.

- [Open six-lens reading guide](https://mercyseries.com/learn/?reading-guide=1): Public explanations, examples and activities; no purchase or sign-in is needed.
- [Book synopsis and editions](https://mercyseries.com/mercy/): Official description and edition information.
- [International companion](https://mercyseries.com/guide/international/): Companion access information for readers after one verified Amazon purchase of MERCY in Kindle, paperback or hardcover.
